pairs.difference: A: the mortarboard is a turned slab seen from slightly above. The top board is a flat, even patch, and the band below sits under it at the same tilt. B: the brim is drawn as a wide open ellipse seen from high above, but the cone and buckle band sit at near eye level and face the viewer. The hat mixes two camera heights, and it floats with no ground.
pairs.fix: Show the witch hat from one slightly raised three-quarter view. The brim should be a narrower ellipse that matches the tilt of the buckle band, and the hat should turn a little to one side.

pairs.difference: A: the plane flies at a strong three-quarter angle. Its nose comes toward the camera, the far wing shrinks with distance, and big foreground clouds overlap the lower right. B: the bat is laid flat in the picture plane. Both wings spread sideways at the same size, the body faces the viewer, and the wings show no foreshortening. The clouds are thin bands behind it with no overlap.
pairs.fix: Turn the bat to three-quarters with its near wing larger and coming toward the camera and its far wing foreshortened behind the body. Add a cloud that overlaps the lower corner.

pairs.difference: A: a low, close camera crops the gloves at the left edge. The near glove overlaps the far one, and the bench plank runs off the card. B: the dead tree is a whole, centered object seen from the front at eye level. It stands on a flat lawn, which ends at a straight horizon behind it, and it has a separate cast shadow, like a staged diorama.
pairs.fix: Bring the camera closer and lower so the trunk and roots fill the lower card and a branch is cropped at the edge. Turn the trunk slightly so one root comes forward over the ground.

pairs.difference: A: the topiary is centered, symmetric and seen from the front. Its pedestal ring is seen from above, but the hedge horizon behind it sits at eye level. B: the slide is turned three-quarters and cropped. The pool deck tiles recede at one consistent angle under the ladder and posts. The topiary's surface reads as noisy leaf texture with no flat faces, at planar share 0.009, below the real range.
pairs.fix: Turn the topiary pot so it is seen slightly from the side. Set the horizon at the same height the pedestal ellipse implies, and let the path recede at that same angle.

pairs.difference: A: the mirror stands square to the camera with left-right symmetric scrolls, while its oval base is seen from above. It reads as a frontal elevation set on a tilted plate. B: the vending machine is turned three-quarters. Its side face is a clean, even plane that recedes with mild convergence, and its feet sit on a floor at eye level.
pairs.fix: Rotate the mirror stand about a quarter turn so one side of the frame and one leg come forward. Show the base ellipse at the same gentle downward angle as the frame.

pairs.difference: A: a low camera looks up at the sign. The motel balcony overlaps on the left and the fence sits behind, giving three depth layers with mild convergence. B: the tower house is a small, complete, centered model on a flat lawn. It is seen from slightly above with every face in one block, and the background treeline sits as a flat strip behind it.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera to just above the grass and crop the house so the tower top nearly touches the card edge. Add a near bush or fence that overlaps the bottom corner.

pairs.difference: A: the gate is seen at an angle. The right pillar is smaller and farther away, and the paving recedes in clear perspective toward the gate, with trees overlapping both sides. B: the iron gate is perfectly frontal and symmetric, with the two pillars the same size. The path is a flat strip straight ahead, and the pillar side faces show as uniform flat slabs (planar share 0.582, above the real range).
pairs.fix: Turn the gate about 20 degrees so one pillar is nearer and larger and the path curves in from a corner. Add foliage in front that overlaps a pillar base.

pairs.difference: A: the sneakers are seen from a raised three-quarter angle. The near shoe overlaps the far one, and the floor-wall seam gives a ground plane. B: the pumpkin sits dead center and faces the camera at eye level. Its face is flat to the viewer, with no turn and a plain gradient floor.
pairs.fix: Turn the pumpkin slightly so its carved face angles off to one side. Raise the camera a little so the top and stem are seen from above.

pairs.difference: A: the fountain is seen from a raised angle. Its basin ellipses all open by a matching amount and sit on paving that recedes in the same perspective. B: the candelabra base is seen nearly side-on, but the table boards slope diagonally across the card at a steeper angle. The holder floats in the middle of the plane, so the table and object don't share one view.
pairs.fix: Make the table top recede level behind the candelabra at the same angle as the base ellipse. Raise the camera slightly so the base's top face shows.

pairs.difference: A: the palm stands in sand dunes, with rocks in the foreground and a soft background spiral. Its ground reads at one level. B: the table edge runs diagonally upward from left to right, so the ground plane is tilted. The ball and its stand sit upright and frontal against that sloped table, which is two different views.
pairs.fix: Make the table edge a level horizontal line behind the stand. Show the stand's ring as an ellipse seen from slightly above, matching the table top.

pairs.difference: A: the broom lies diagonally, flat in the picture plane. The handle tip and bristles are the same scale, so there is no foreshortening along its length, and the clouds are only a low band. B: the balloons overlap one another, with the front teal balloon in front of the others. The strings converge to a knot, giving some depth order.
pairs.fix: Point the broom handle back into the distance so its far end narrows, with the bristle head larger and nearer the camera. Add a cloud overlapping the handle.

pairs.difference: A: the clock is a flat-on wall object, which matches the real card. B: the plinth is seen from a high three-quarter angle with strongly converging steps, but the lion's head turns straight to the camera at eye level. The path and trees also recede at a different angle from the plinth, giving mixed viewpoints and a stronger, wide-angle perspective.
pairs.fix: Use one mild three-quarter view for the whole statue so the lion's head turns with the plinth. Flatten the step convergence, and set the path to recede at the same angle as the plinth edges.

pattern: Generated cards show the object whole and centered, as a front-facing or symmetric model on a separate, often tilted ground plane, viewed from a camera height that doesn't match the object. Base ellipses are seen from above while the body is seen at eye level. Real cards use one mild three-quarter turn, crop the object or bring it close, and overlap foreground over background so the layers read in depth.
